subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Gotthard Base Tunnel
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Gotthard Base Tunnel usable.

hook.text: The world's longest rail tunnel — 35.5 miles through the Swiss Alps, 1.4 miles underground.

buildup.text: Four TBMs and extensive drill-and-blast excavated 28 million tons of rock over 17 years.

discovery.text: Rock temperatures reached 115°F at maximum depth — workers needed cooling systems.

twist.text: Trains now cross the Alps on a flat line — no winding mountain passes, no steep gradients.

climax.text: It cut Zurich to Milan travel from 3.5 hours to 2.5 — shifting freight from trucks to rail.

punchline.text: Go through the mountain instead of over it. Seventeen years to remove a barrier.

quiz.question: What was a major challenge of tunneling deep under the Alps for the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
options: Extreme cold temperatures froze the equipment underground
Rock temperatures reached 115°F at maximum depth, requiring cooling systems
The tunnel flooded with alpine snowmelt every spring

details.summary: The Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland is the world's longest railway tunnel at 57 kilometers, passing beneath the Alps at a maximum depth of 2,300 meters below the mountain surface.
details.whyItMatters: The Gotthard Base Tunnel represents the pinnacle of tunnel engineering achievement. It shifted freight from road to rail through the Alps and set new standards for deep tunnel construction in extreme conditions.
takeaways: At 57 kilometers, it is the world's longest and deepest railway tunnel
Rock temperatures reached 45 degrees Celsius at maximum depth of 2,300 meters
The flat alignment allows trains to cross the Alps without steep grades or winding curves

faq.question: What extreme conditions did engineers face at 2,300 meters depth?
faq.answer: Rock temperatures reached 45 degrees Celsius from geothermal heat. Rock pressures were enormous, requiring heavy support in some zones. Massive refrigeration systems cooled the working environment.

faq.question: How does the Gotthard Base Tunnel benefit freight transportation?
faq.answer: The flat alignment allows heavy freight trains to cross the Alps without the steep grades that limited train length and required multiple locomotives on the old route. Transit times dropped significantly.
